A.depoimento: I am sending my entire current army to capture the neutral village of Santarem, while ordering the capital to produce two more spearmen to begin rebuilding our forces for the next push.
A.plano: Capture Santarem to expand north towards Coimbra and Porto. Build up troops in Lisboa to maintain the capital's garrison while expanding. Next targets after Santarem will be Coimbra and Badajoz to secure the northern route.

A.depoimento: I order the construction of 2 spearmen in Lisboa and launch a full-scale attack on Coimbra with my Santarem garrison. The neutral archer garrison should fall quickly, expanding my territory and bringing me closer to victory.
A.plano: Capture Coimbra this turn to expand north. Next turn, capture Evora with the 4 spearmen now building in Lisboa. Then push towards Porto, Salamanca, and Badajoz to secure the northern and eastern routes. Build up troops in each captured village to maintain momentum and eventually reach the 18-village threshold.

B.depoimento: We attacked the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona with our army, sending archers and a knight to Tarragona and spearmen and a knight to Girona. We also built more spearmen at home. Our forces should easily overcome the weak defenses and we will add these villages to our kingdom.
B.plano: Capture the neutral villages Tarragona and Girona to expand our territory. Next turn, build troops at all three villages and send armies to explore and conquer more neutrals. Aim to reach 18 villages quickly. Keep a small garrison at Barcelona and watch for enemy movements.

A.depoimento: I ordered a double attack on Evora and Porto to expand my kingdom. My Lisbon spearmen marched on Evora, while my full Coimbra army took Porto. I'm also building an archer in Lisbon and two spearmen in Santarem to strengthen my forces for the next campaign.
A.plano: Capture Evora and Porto this turn to expand my territory. Next turn, I will build troops in all my villages and send reinforcements from Santarem to Coimbra. I will explore the map from my new villages: Faro from Evora, and Vigo/Salamanca from Porto. My goal is to secure the western coast and push inland to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: My brave generals, the time for expansion is now! We strike on three fronts simultaneously: Tarragona splits its arrows to shatter Castellon and Zaragoza, while Girona's spear and charge overwhelm Huesca. Barcelona forges a fresh knight and rushes spearman reinforcements to our newly won borders. By sunset, our banner flies over six villages! Onwards to victory!
B.plano: Launch a triple attack to conquer Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca simultaneously. Split Tarragona's forces to take Castellon and Zaragoza, while Girona assaults Huesca. Barcelona will produce a knight and send spearman reinforcements to Tarragona and Girona to secure our new borders. Next turn, we will push deeper into the unexplored roads toward Madrid and Valencia.

B.depoimento: This turn we focus on strengthening our forward positions. Tarragona sends spearmen to Castellon to ready our southern assault, while Barcelona reinforces Zaragoza with an archer. Our builders work diligently, producing spearmen in Tarragona and Girona, and an archer in Barcelona, ensuring our armies grow as we project power deeper into the map.
B.plano: Reinforce Castellon with 2 spearman from Tarragona to prepare for the attack on Valencia. Barcelona sends its archer to Zaragoza to build up forces for Madrid. We build spearmen in Tarragona and Girona, and an archer in Barcelona to replenish our ranks. Next turn, launch the Valencia assault from Castellon with the reinforced garrison; continue building for the Madrid push.

A.depoimento: I order the elite garrison of Porto to march on Vigo, confident in our numbers and the weakness of the neutral defenders. Meanwhile, our blacksmiths work tirelessly, forging spearmen in Coimbra and Santarem, and knights in Lisboa, to strengthen our army for the campaigns to come.
A.plano: Expand north to Vigo to secure a coastal foothold and resource boost. Build spearmen in Coimbra and Santarem to prepare for future attacks towards Madrid and Toledo. Build knights in Lisboa for fast strike capability. Next turns, attack Salamanca from Coimbra/Porto and push towards Madrid.

B.depoimento: We have marshaled our forces for a two-pronged attack. All archers are converging on Castellon to strike Valencia, while spearman and knights gather at Zaragoza to take Teruel. Our villages are building archers to sustain the war effort. The enemy remains unseen, but we must press our advantage.
B.plano: Plan: Concentrate archers on Castellon for Valencia. All available archers sent to Castellon; we built archers in every village. All spearman and knights moved to Zaragoza to form a spearman army for Teruel. Next turn, Castellon will only have the newly built archer; wait for reinforcements to arrive before ordering the Valencia assault. Continue building archers in Castellon and Zaragoza. Keep watching for enemy movements.

A.depoimento: The army from Vigo marches on Burgos to secure our northern flank. In the south, we are massing troops in Santarem, Coimbra, Evora, and Porto. Lisboa's elite archers and knights ride to Santarem to prepare for the push into Badajoz. The war for the peninsula is underway!
A.plano: Attack Burgos from Vigo to expand north and secure a staging ground for Madrid. Build spearmen in Santarem, Coimbra, Evora, and Porto to swell the ranks. Send Lisboa's archer and knight to Santarem to prepare for the attack on Badajoz. After securing Burgos and Badajoz, push towards Madrid and Toledo to reach the enemy capital.

B.depoimento: I have launched a three-pronged attack: my archers take Valencia, my spearman storm Madrid, and my knights ride to Pamplona. With these captures, I raise my banner over nine villages. The enemy remains unseen, but I will strengthen my new lands and prepare for the next push.
B.plano: We are attacking Valencia with all 5 archers from Castellon, Madrid with 11 spearman from Zaragoza, and Pamplona with 3 knights from Zaragoza. We aim to capture 3 neutrals to reach 9 villages. We must rebuild troops: Castellon builds 3 archers, Zaragoza builds 2 archers and 2 spearman. Next turn, we will assess losses, reinforce new villages, and plan to capture Teruel. Do not attack Lisboa yet.

A.depoimento: Our armies have struck at Badajoz and Pamplona, sweeping aside the neutral garrisons to expand our borders. In the capital and other cities, the forges are burning day and night, churning out knights to swell our ranks. We march towards total dominance!
A.plano: Expand into neutral territories to boost economy and army. This turn, attack Badajoz from Santarem and Pamplona from Burgos with full forces. Simultaneously, build knights in all major cities to prepare for the next wave. Send the newly built knights from Lisboa to Evora to reinforce the upcoming attack on Faro. Next turn, conquer Faro and Salamanca, then push towards Madrid.

B.depoimento: King B's forces struck hard this turn, launching a three-pronged attack on the neutral villages of Murcia, Teruel, and Pamplona. Valencia's archers swept through Murcia, while Zaragoza's mixed force took Teruel, and the remaining archers captured Pamplona. The army is now poised to expand further, with the northern villages building a steady stream of knights to secure the realm.
B.plano: We attacked Murcia, Teruel, and Pamplona this turn. We must rebuild troops in Zaragoza and Madrid for the next wave. Next turn, we will assess the losses in the new villages and plan to attack Salamanca and Toledo. Do not attack the enemy capital yet. Focus on consolidating the north and preparing for the push south.

A.depoimento: My armies struck on all fronts this turn. From the south, Evora's knights took Faro; from the north, Porto's spearmen and knights overwhelmed Salamanca; from the center, Badajoz's forces conquered Toledo; and in the east, Pamplona's knight captured Zaragoza. With four new villages, my kingdom grows stronger.
A.plano: This turn, conquer Faro, Salamanca, Toledo, and Zaragoza to reach 13 villages. Next turn, attack Sevilha from Badajoz, Madrid from Toledo, and Huesca from Zaragoza. Continue building troops and sending reinforcements to the front lines. Explore the unexplored eastern territories to find the enemy capital and secure more villages. Aim for 18 villages or total enemy elimination.

B.depoimento: We launched a coordinated attack on Burgos and Pamplona, while sending archers to reinforce our army at Teruel. Our forces are rebuilding for the next phase of expansion.
B.plano: We are attacking Burgos with 5 spearmen from Madrid (leaving 1 for defense) and Pamplona with all troops from Huesca. We reinforce the marching army at Teruel with 5 archers from Castellon. All villages are building troops to rebuild our forces. Next turn, we will assess losses and plan attacks on Salamanca, Toledo, and Cordoba. Do not attack the enemy capital yet. Focus on consolidating the north and pushing south.

B.depoimento: Turn 10 is a turning point for our kingdom. We have consolidated our forces and launched a coordinated double attack. The army from Teruel is marching on Toledo, while the northern army is poised to conquer Pamplona. We have gathered the strength of our interior villages to flood Zaragoza with reinforcements, preparing for the next phase of the campaign. The losses at Burgos are avenged, and we are on the move to reclaim the map.
B.plano: We are launching a decisive double attack: the Teruel army is marching on Toledo to secure the southern border, while the northern army is set to conquer Pamplona next turn. We have gathered reinforcements from our interior villages to flood Zaragoza, preparing for the next push into enemy territory. We are rebuilding our forces with knights and archers in all viable villages. Next turn, we will assess the outcomes of the Toledo and Pamplona battles and plan the conquest of Burgos and Salamanca.

A.depoimento: I attacked Madrid with knights and spearmen from Salamanca and Burgos, taking the enemy village. I moved knights to Badajoz and Salamanca to secure the borders and prepare for attacks on Toledo and Sevilha. I built new archers and knights across my realm.
A.plano: Capture Madrid this turn with Salamanca and Burgos forces. Reinforce Badajoz with knights from Evora, Santarem, Faro to build a strike force for Toledo. Build archers for Sevilha. Next turn, attack Sevilha with archers and Toledo with knights. Then expand south to Cordoba and neutral villages. Aim for 18 villages.

A.depoimento: Order the assault on Toledo with the full might of Badajoz's cavalry. Simultaneously, I am stripping my interior villages to send every available knight and archer to the front lines, ensuring Badajoz becomes an unassailable fortress the moment Toledo falls. Madrid and Burgos are also being reinforced to hold the eastern flank against Zaragoza and Pamplona. We build knights across the realm to fuel our expansion. The march to 18 villages begins now!
A.plano: Conquer Toledo this turn with Badajoz's knights and archers. Reinforce Badajoz with all available knights and archers from Evora, Santarem, Faro, Salamanca, Coimbra, Lisboa, Porto to build a massive strike force for the next moves. Reinforce Madrid with spearmen and knight from Salamanca, and Burgos with knights from Madrid and Vigo. Build knights in all major villages to grow our cavalry. Next turn, attack Sevilha with the accumulated force in Badajoz, and secure the southern front. Then push towards Cordoba and the neutral villages to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: King B has ordered a triple strike! Our armies from Toledo, Zaragoza, and Pamplona are marching on Cordoba, Madrid, and Burgos respectively. We have built a massive number of knights and archers across our empire to support this offensive. If our plans succeed, we will expand our kingdom significantly and move closer to victory!
B.plano: Attack Cordoba [11] from Toledo [8], Madrid [12] from Zaragoza [17], and Burgos [14] from Pamplona [19] to conquer three villages this turn. Do not attack Badajoz [4] yet as its defense is too high (25). Focus on building knights and archers in all villages to maximize our army's strength and prepare for the next wave of expansions.

A.depoimento: The legions of Badajoz march to Toledo, ready to strike at the heart of the enemy's domain. From every province, knights ride to Salamanca, their steel gleaming in the sun, to counter the enemy's archers at Madrid. Our forges burn day and night, crafting the weapons of victory. The enemy's time is running out.
A.plano: Reinforce Toledo with the army of Badajoz and gather knights at Salamanca. Next turn, attack Teruel from Toledo and Madrid from Salamanca. The knight-heavy force at Salamanca will counter the enemy's archers, while the overwhelming host from Toledo will crush Teruel. After taking these, push towards Valencia and the enemy capital, while building more troops to maintain the offensive.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered my armies to strike at Salamanca, Vigo, and the neutral Sevilha. My forces in Burgos swept aside Vigo, while my archers and knights took Salamanca and Sevilha. Reinforcements from the interior marched to reinforce the border villages. The path to victory grows shorter.
B.plano: We launched attacks on Salamanca, Vigo, and Sevilha to capture them. Reinforcements sent from interior villages to border villages to defend and prepare for next expansion. Next turn, we must check if we captured those villages, then send troops to garrison them and plan attacks on Coimbra, Porto, and Faro. Also watch for enemy counterattacks on Madrid, Cordoba, and Teruel.

A.depoimento: King A launches a massive three-pronged attack this turn. Toledo sends its main force to Teruel, Salamanca strikes Madrid, and Badajoz takes Sevilha. Simultaneously, I reinforce my borders: Vigo gets archers from Porto, Badajoz gets spearmen from Faro, and Salamanca gets troops from Coimbra. My villages are busy building knights and archers to sustain the offensive. The enemy is caught off guard as my armies converge on their key positions.
A.plano: Attack Teruel from Toledo, Madrid from Salamanca, and Sevilha from Badajoz this turn. Reinforce Vigo with Porto's archers, Badajoz with Faro's spearmen, and Salamanca with Coimbra's troops. Build knights and archers everywhere to rebuild the army. After conquering these three, push towards Valencia and the enemy capital to secure the win.

A.depoimento: My armies attack on three fronts this turn. From Teruel, I strike Valencia with knights and archers. From Toledo, I march on Cordoba. From Vigo, I assault Burgos. I also reinforce my vulnerable border villages of Sevilha and Madrid, and send Porto's knight to Vigo. My builders work overtime, producing knights and archers in every village to swell my ranks.
A.plano: Conquer Valencia, Cordoba, and Burgos this turn to expand on three fronts. Next turn, take Castellon from the east and Zaragoza from the center to reach 18 villages. Build knights and archers everywhere to maintain momentum. Focus on the weak enemy villages first and avoid the capital for now, aiming to hold 75% of the map for 2 turns.

B.depoimento: I have ordered my archers and knights from Cordoba to strike Sevilha, while Zaragoza's spearmen and knights march on Madrid. Simultaneously, I am reinforcing my borders: Pamplona sends troops to Burgos, Tarragona to Castellon, and Girona to Barcelona. My aim is to secure these two easy victories and consolidate my forces for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Attacking Sevilha [9] with Cordoba's archers and knights, and Madrid [12] with Zaragoza's spearmen and knights. Reinforcing Burgos [14] from Pamplona, Castellon [18] from Tarragona, and Barcelona [22] from Girona. Next turn, if I conquer Sevilha and Madrid, I will have 13 villages. I should then plan the next attacks: from Sevilha to Badajoz [4] or Faro [5], and from Madrid to Salamanca [7] or Toledo [8]. Also, keep an eye on Vigo [10] from Burgos.

A.depoimento: I have launched decisive attacks on Madrid and Murcia, leveraging the counter triangle to crush the enemy defenses. My armies are pushing on two fronts, while I reinforce Faro, Vigo, and Teruel to secure my borders. The enemy's attempt on Sevilha has failed, and I will finish it next turn. I am building knights and archers to maintain my war machine.
A.plano: This turn, I attack Madrid from Salamanca and Murcia from Cordoba, using counter bonuses to minimize losses. Next turn, I will send knights from Cordoba to take Sevilha after the failed assault, and I will attack Burgos from Madrid after it falls. I will continue to reinforce my border villages (Faro, Vigo, Teruel) to prevent enemy incursions. My goal is to reach 18 villages by turn 20 and hold them for 2 turns to win. I am building archers and knights everywhere to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: King A has ordered a decisive triple strike! Knights from Cordoba and Teruel march to crush Sevilha and Zaragoza, while Vigo's finest storm Burgos. In a brilliant strategic move, Porto's knight is sent to reinforce Vigo's defenses. With these victories, the King will rule 18 villages, bringing the enemy to its knees!
A.plano: This turn, I launch a three-pronged offensive to conquer Sevilha, Zaragoza, and Burgos, bringing my total to 18 villages to secure the 75% win condition. I send knights from Cordoba and Teruel to exploit the archer counter, and a mixed force from Vigo to take Burgos. I will also reinforce Vigo from Porto. Next turn, I will consolidate my new territories, build up armies, and push towards the enemy capital if needed.

B.depoimento: This turn, King B orders a massive offensive! The armies of Zaragoza and Burgos march on Madrid, while the elite of Castellon strike at Valencia. Reinforcements from Huesca, Tarragona, and Barcelona flow to secure our borders. We build troops in every village, ready for the next battle!
B.plano: We are launching a double-pronged attack to conquer Madrid and Valencia this turn. We are sending all troops from Zaragoza and Burgos to Madrid, and all troops from Castellon to Valencia. We are reinforcing Zaragoza with Huesca's troops, and Castellon with Tarragona and Barcelona's troops to keep our borders strong. We are building troops in all our villages to grow our army.

A.depoimento: I have ordered a massive offensive on the enemy borders. Salamanca's army marches on Madrid, Toledo's knights ride to Teruel to prepare the attack on Valencia, and Vigo's cavalry reinforces Burgos for the assault on Pamplona. My villages are building reinforcements to secure our hold on the map.
A.plano: Conquer Madrid, Valencia, and Pamplona to reach 18 villages. Send Salamanca's garrison to attack Madrid. Send Toledo's knights to Teruel to prepare for Valencia. Send Vigo's knights to Burgos to prepare for Pamplona next turn. Reinforce Salamanca and Toledo from Coimbra and Cordoba. Build troops in all major villages.

B.depoimento: I launched a massive offensive on four fronts, targeting Murcia, Teruel, Burgos, and Salamanca. My armies achieved victories across the board, leveraging counter bonuses to overcome the enemy's defenses. I also reinforced Zaragoza and began rebuilding my forces for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Conquering Murcia, Teruel, Burgos, and Salamanca this turn to expand my territory. Reinforcing Zaragoza with Tarragona and Huesca. Building troops across all villages to maintain momentum. Next turn, focus on Toledo and Cordoba.

A.depoimento: I have ordered full-scale assaults on five enemy villages simultaneously. My armies from Badajoz, Toledo, Cordoba, Teruel, and Burgos march on Salamanca, Madrid, Murcia, Valencia, and Pamplona. If these attacks succeed, I will command 18 villages and be on the threshold of victory. I have also ordered troop production in all my cities to sustain the campaign.
A.plano: Launch simultaneous all-out attacks on the five weakest enemy villages: Salamanca, Madrid, Murcia, Valencia, and Pamplona. Send every available troop from Badajoz, Toledo, Cordoba, Teruel, and Burgos. If all attacks succeed, I will hold 18 villages and be on the verge of victory. Next turn, focus on rebuilding the emptied villages, fortifying new borders, and preparing for enemy counter-attacks. Continue building troops in all villages to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: Turn 20: I order Salamanca's garrison to march on Porto and conquer it, adding to my domain. I send reinforcements from Zaragoza to Madrid and from Valencia to Murcia to prepare for the next attacks on Burgos and Cordoba. All my villages are building troops to swell my armies.
B.plano: Taking Porto with Salamanca. Reinforcing Madrid from Zaragoza and Murcia from Valencia to prepare attacks on Burgos and Cordoba next turn. Building troops everywhere. Next turn: attack Burgos and Cordoba.

A.depoimento: Salamanca is mine — the Badajoz vanguard crushes the thin garrison. In the east, Valencia's archers and knights ride to Murcia, where the counter bonus carries the day. Madrid holds against my doomed Toledo assault, but I care little: two more villages fall this turn and I stand at the threshold of victory. One more target and the crown is mine.
A.plano: Salamanca falls this turn (arriving attack from Badajoz), giving me 16 villages. I attack Murcia from Valencia with 3 archers and 4 knights — my knight-heavy force triggers the counter bonus against their archers, giving me the edge to take it. If both succeed, I reach 17 villages. Next turn I will flood Pamplona with reinforcements from Burgos and Vigo, then launch the Huesca assault to hit 18. After that I must hold 18 for two consecutive turns to win — I'll fortify the new borders (Salamanca-Madrid, Murcia-Castellon) and keep building in every village to replace losses and deter counter-att

A.depoimento: My armies have secured Salamanca and Murcia, bringing my total to 17 villages. Today, I launch the decisive assault on Huesca from Pamplona to reach the 18-village threshold. I am reinforcing my borders at Salamanca and Toledo to deter enemy counter-attacks. If Huesca falls, I will be one step away from victory, needing only to hold my gains for two turns.
A.plano: Huesca is the key to reaching 18 villages. I will launch the assault from Pamplona this turn, sending all available troops. To secure the border, I am reinforcing Pamplona from Burgos, moving Vigo's knights to Burgos as a second wave, and strengthening Salamanca and Toledo against potential Madrid counter-attacks. Once Huesca falls, I will have 18 villages and must hold them for two consecutive turns to win. I will focus on building archers and knights to replace losses and maintain pressure on Zaragoza and Castellon.

B.depoimento: This turn, King B launches a coordinated multi-front offensive to expand our empire. Our brave armies from Madrid, Zaragoza, and Castellon march to conquer the weakly defended enemy villages of Burgos, Teruel, and Valencia respectively. In parallel, we reinforce our northern border at Huesca from Girona and bolster our eastern defenses by shifting troops from the interior to Castellon. We are confident that these decisive actions will secure our victory and bring us closer to ruling 75% of the map!
B.plano: Focus on expanding our territory by conquering the weak enemy border villages: Burgos, Teruel, and Valencia. Simultaneously reinforce our vulnerable border village Huesca from Girona, and shift troops from our interior villages (Tarragona, Barcelona) to strengthen our border defenses at Castellon. Keep a balanced garrison in Madrid to protect our capital region. Build troops across all villages to maintain growth and replenish losses.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch a multi-pronged offensive to secure our borders and expand our territory. We send a strong force from Madrid to conquer Toledo, and a veteran garrison from Burgos to take Pamplona. To defend against the enemy's thrust at Huesca, we rush reinforcements from Girona and Zaragoza. Meanwhile, our army at Teruel is set to conquer it next turn, and we probe Murcia from Valencia while reinforcing our frontline villages. We must hold the line and grow our army for the push to 18 villages.
B.plano: Focus on expanding our territory by conquering the weak enemy border villages: Pamplona, Toledo, and Murcia. Simultaneously reinforce our vulnerable border village Huesca from Girona and Zaragoza to defend against the incoming enemy army. Shift troops from our interior villages (Barcelona, Tarragona) to strengthen our border defenses at Castellon and Zaragoza. Keep a balanced garrison in Madrid to protect our capital region. Build troops across all villages to maintain growth and replenish losses.

A.depoimento: I reinforced Toledo to hold the line against the enemy's counter-attack, while my spearhead forces struck at Madrid and Burgos, sweeping away their weak garrisons and expanding my domain.
A.plano: Defend Toledo from the incoming enemy army by reinforcing it from Badajoz and Cordoba. Simultaneously, launch a double offensive: attack Madrid from Salamanca and Burgos from Vigo to secure two easy villages and bring my total to 16. Rebuild troops in the core villages for the next push towards Teruel and Valencia.

A.depoimento: My armies strike on three fronts simultaneously. The knight from Madrid takes Burgos, the archers and knight from Toledo assault Teruel, and the Murcian forces capture Valencia. With these three victories, I will hold 18 villages and be one step away from total dominance. My troops are ordered to leave enough defenders in the border villages to hold the line while the enemy is crushed on the roads.
A.plano: Capture Burgos, Teruel, and Valencia this turn to reach 18 villages. Send 1 knight from Madrid to Burgos, 5 archers and 1 knight from Toledo to Teruel, and 1 archer and 4 knights from Murcia to Valencia. Rebuild troops in all core villages, focusing on archers and knights, to secure the new territories and prepare for the next push towards Zaragoza and the enemy capital Barcelona.

B.depoimento: We are launching a multi-pronged offensive. Vigo is undefended, and Pamplona is weak, so we are taking them. We are also reinforcing our border villages to prepare for attacks on Madrid and Murcia next turn.
B.plano: Capture the empty village of Vigo and the weak Pamplona this turn. Reinforce Zaragoza, Valencia, and Teruel to prepare for attacks on Madrid and Murcia next turn. Build troops to replenish losses and increase our army size.

A.depoimento: I am launching a coordinated assault on Burgos and Teruel. My Madrid garrison will send a strong knight-led force to overrun Burgos, while Toledo's archers and knights will strike Teruel with the counter bonus. I am reinforcing my border villages to secure the gains and prepare for the next push towards Valencia and Zaragoza.
A.plano: Capture Burgos and Teruel this turn to reach 18 villages. Attack Burgos with knights and archers from Madrid, and Teruel with knights and archers from Toledo using the counter bonus. Reinforce Madrid and Toledo with troops from Salamanca, Badajoz, and Cordoba to hold the new borders. Next, push towards Valencia and Zaragoza, and eventually the enemy capital Barcelona. Rebuild troops in all core villages, focusing on knights and archers.

B.depoimento: King B orders the general mobilization! Our armies march on Madrid, Murcia, Pamplona, and Vigo simultaneously. By using the ancient spear-and-knight tactics, we break their defenses. The peninsula will soon be ours!
B.plano: Launch a massive multi-front offensive this turn to conquer Madrid, Murcia, Pamplona, and Vigo. Use the counter triangle strategy to defeat Madrid (spearman vs knight) and Vigo (knights vs archers). Send a second wave to Pamplona to ensure its capture. Reinforce Teruel, Valencia, Huesca, and Zaragoza for future turns. Build troops in all villages to replenish our army.

A.depoimento: Ordered the assault on Madrid with Toledo's archers, exploiting the counter bonus. Reinforced Pamplona and Cordoba to secure the borders. Spearmen are marching north to target the enemy's northern villages. The push toward 18 villages continues.
A.plano: Capture Madrid this turn with 8 archers from Toledo to reach 15 villages. Reinforce Pamplona from Burgos to hold against the enemy army arriving, and send Sevilha's troops to Cordoba to prepare for Murcia. Start marching spearmen from Santarem and Lisboa toward the north for future attacks on Zaragoza/Huesca. Rebuild troops focusing on knights for Teruel/Murcia and archers for defense. Next targets: Teruel and Murcia.

B.depoimento: My armies strike on multiple fronts today! Madrid splits its forces to take the weak garrison of Salamanca and the richer prize of Burgos. Murcia moves on Cordoba, while Zaragoza sends a fast reinforcement to Pamplona. We are building troops across the realm to secure our borders and prepare for the final push to 18 villages!
B.plano: Conquer Salamanca, Burgos, Cordoba, and Pamplona. Split Madrid's troops: 2/2/2 to Burgos, 1/1/1 to Salamanca. Send Zaragoza's 2 archers, 4 knights to Pamplona for reinforcement. Build troops in all villages to replenish losses and prepare for the push into Toledo and the north.

B.depoimento: Turn 28: I ordered a multi-pronged expansion. My army in Teruel attacks the weakly defended Toledo, while I send reinforcements to Murcia to secure the southern border against Cordoba. The northern borders of Zaragoza and Burgos are reinforced with troops from the rear. I also ordered troop production in all villages to replenish my forces.
B.plano: Plan: I am attacking Toledo from Teruel to break the southern front. I am reinforcing Murcia with Valencia's troops to prevent a Cordoba counter-attack. I am moving all rear troops to the borders: Barcelona, Tarragona, Girona, Huesca to Zaragoza; Pamplona to Burgos. I left 2 knights in Teruel for defense. I built knights and archers everywhere. Next turn: check if Toledo fell, then attack Madrid or Vigo. Do not attack Cordoba yet, it's too strong.

A.depoimento: I have ordered a massive build-up of spearman and knights across my realm. The strike force from Cordoba, supported by Madrid and Badajoz, will take Toledo this turn. Meanwhile, reinforcements flow to the northern and southern fronts to keep the pressure on King B's remaining strongholds.
A.plano: Focus on capturing Toledo this turn with knights from Cordoba, archers from Madrid, and mixed troops from Badajoz. Simultaneously, reinforce Madrid from Salamanca, Cordoba from Sevilha, and Vigo from Porto to prepare for attacks on Burgos, Murcia, and Zaragoza in the coming turns. Build a balanced mix of spearman and knights in all villages to maintain offensive capability.

B.depoimento: Our armies have struck at the enemy on three fronts. Knights from Zaragoza, Burgos, and Toledo have surged forward to take Madrid, Vigo, and Badajoz. Reinforcements have been dispatched to strengthen our borders and prepare for the next push. The war for the peninsula has begun in earnest.
B.plano: We launched attacks on Madrid, Vigo, and Badajoz with knights. We reinforced Toledo with Teruel's knights and moved interior knights to Zaragoza. We built knights and archers across our territory. Next turn, check if our attacks succeeded. If Madrid fell, push to Salamanca. If Vigo fell, move on Porto. If Badajoz fell, secure route to Sevilha. Then focus on Cordoba from Toledo. Keep building knights. Do not attack Cordoba until we have enough knights to lead with counter.

A.depoimento: Orders issued for a double-pronged assault on Toledo and Burgos, leveraging our numerical advantage. Reinforcements are flowing to Salamanca and Cordoba to prepare for the next phase of the campaign against Madrid and Murcia.
